text:
sam (eng-platform): heads-up — I'm prototyping a 'Why this cost?' tooltip for the model-cost sparkline on the Console. idea: show breakdown between raw token burn, cache savings (amortized), and routing delta. thoughts?

lina (product): love it. users keep asking why two tenants with same token counts show different costs. tooltips could be the first-line explainability. :eyes:

matt (eng-ml): +1. need to be careful how we show amortized cache savings — it's easy to confuse customers if we use exact cents. maybe show percent + example invocation equivalence instead of dollars?

raj (eng-platform): implementation note: we already emit per-request attributes: token_count, cache_hit_bytes, model_variant. we don't currently emit amortized_prefetch_credit on the sampled ingest. can we derive it offline?

sam (eng-platform): proposal: compute a per-tenant amortized cache credit in nightly job and surface the estimate in tooltip with a small confidence badge. realtime hover just shows last-24h estimate and link to "how we compute it".

jess (design): keep tooltip light. 3 lines max: 1) token burn, 2) cache saved (est.), 3) routing surcharge (if any). link to modal for full explainability. use microcopy: "estimated" where needed.

ben (finance): please include "model SKU" in tooltip. when routing falls back from v2 to v1 we see ~30% cost delta and customers ask for that explicitly. also: optional toggle to show dollars vs normalized tokens for customers on prepay.

matt (eng-ml): +1 on sku. also flag edgecase: shared-prefetch between tenants -> attribution ambiguity. should call out when >10% of savings are shared across tenants.

raj (eng-platform): question for Sam: how do we handle quota interactions? e.g., if quota triggers routing to cheaper variant, tooltip should show "quota routed" reason not just cost delta. otherwise customers will be confused when their app hits quota and costs drop.

sam (eng-platform): good catch. adding a short reason field: one of ["normal", "quota_reroute", "region_fallback", "manual_override"]. small enum string in the tooltip.

lina (product): what about auditability? customers want to download a CSV of these explainability rows for billing disputes. track the tooltip breakdown in the billing export?

ben (finance): yes please. add columns: token_burn, cache_credit_est, routing_reason, model_sku, sample_rate. even if some are estimated, they should be present.

raj (eng-platform): implementation constraints: adding extra columns to billing export is fine, but we need to keep payload small. suggest we only add per-tenant aggregated rows (daily) not per-invocation. we already store per-invocation in traces for a short retention.

jess (design): UX question — when confidence is low (sampled data), show a yellow dot + tooltip "low confidence" and a short inline explanation for what that means. users hate surprises.

sam (eng-platform): plan of attack: 1) api: augment /v1/tenant/costs?range=24h to return aggregated breakdown with a flag "derived_from_sample". 2) nightly job to produce amortized_prefetch_credit per tenant. 3) console: tooltip UI + modal + csv link. 4) docs: short explainer + math appendix.

matt (eng-ml): for (2) we should use the existing prefetch lineage table and weight by observed hit-rate. I'll drop a draft query in here later.

raj (eng-platform): perf note: console hover should not call a heavy endpoint. prefetch the aggregated small blob with the costs card payload.

ops-bot: deploy queued — cost-tooltip-service v1.0 -> staging. initiated by @sam. :robot_face:

lina (product): timelines?

sam (eng-platform): aiming for an internal beta next week (staging only). will post PRs for api + job. if QA is green we'll roll to canary the week after.

ben (finance): assign me to beta so I can sanity-check numbers before canary.

jess (design): I'll mock the tooltip variants in Figma and share. small ask: include the routing_reason icon so it's scannable.

sam (eng-platform): thanks team — I'll open the RFC and link to this thread. if anyone wants to add a use-case or examples to the docs section please drop them in the RFC. :thumbsup:
